upa: This grammar is found in two ways: as a nibb ပါတ်na and as an upasagga. There, the Upaddha, the Nibb နိna, is described as "Upanitavayo-ti Upapati Nipatamatta" (Dhamma, II, 216). It is opened as a meaningless Padalinkara. The meanings and meanings of the parables are: See original.
upabbaje: [Upa+vaja+a+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should approach. See - Upabbajati.
upabbajeyya: [Upa+vaja+a+dhayya] (kri) CL=7 You should approach. See - Upabbajati.
upabhoga: [Upa+bhuja+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 (1) The requisite or article or physical basis that is profitable and useful. Utensils. (2) Enjoying or using.
upabhogabhaṇḍa: [Upabhoga+bhaṇḍa] (na) CL=7 The physical basis that is profitable and useful.
upabhogajāta: [Upabhoga+jāta] (ti) CL=7 That is utensil or requisite or physical basis.
upabhogaparibhoga:
[Upabhoga+paribhoga]  CL=7 The term upabhogaparibhoga refers to materials for enjoyment and use, categorized into two types: (1)
Upabhoga: Interior or personal properties, such as garments, rings, and beads, which are used by individuals temporarily or directly. (2) Paribhoga: Exterior or shared properties, such as buildings, tools, or facilities, which are used frequently and communally. (3) Living beings are termed Upabhoga because they are used or enjoyed in proximity. (4) Non-living objects are termed Paribhoga because they are used frequently and in a general capacity. (5) A person worthy of obtaining these properties (interior or exterior) is one suitable for receiving such items as garments, rings, or facilities, due to their appropriateness or merit.
Upabhogaparibhoga(pu) [upabhogaparibhoga+araha] (Visuddhi, sya. 3. 107).

upabhogāraha: [Upabhoga+araha] (ti) CL=7 Worthy to use or enjoy.

upabhuñjanaka: [Upa+bhuja+ṇvu] (ti) CL=7 [Anakapru, dhāna, ṭī. 167. Upa+bhuja+aka. Na-lā. Nirutti, nhā. 546.] One who enjoys. See - Upabhuñjanakavatthusampadā.
upabhuñjanakavatthusampadā: [Upabhuñjanakavatthu+sampadā] (thī) CL=7 The fulfillment of an object that is a person who enjoys.

upabrūhanaparivāra: [Upabrūhana+parivāra] (pu) CL=7 The dhamma that is surrounded by the function of development or augmentation.

upabrūhayamāna: [Upa+brūha+ṇaya+māna] (ti) CL=7 One who increases or causes to increase.

upabrūhenti: [Upa+brūha+ṇe+anti] (kā,kri) CL=7 They increase or cause to increase. See - Upabrūheti.
upabrūhita: [Upa+brūha+ṇe+ta]  CL=9 That should be increased. Increasing or developing.
upabrūhitañāṇa: [Upabrūhita+ñāṇa] (ti) CL=7 One who has a wisdom that increases or develops.
upacaritabba: [Upa+cara+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be spoken or taught.

upaccakā: [Upa+ccaka] (thī) CL=7 [Selassādho-bhāgāsannabhūmi upaccakānāma, atra tehi upādisaddehi ccako yadādinā. Dhāna,ṭī. 610]. The land of the base of a mountain. The land that is near the base of a mountain.
upaccheda: [Upa+chida+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 (A) Breaking. Completely stop. Destruction. (B) Cutting off.
upacchedaka: [Upa+chida+ṇvu] (na) CL=7 (1) Kamma that approaches and destroys. A Kamma that approaches and destroys a weak kamma and the consequence of that weak kamma. Upacchedakakamma. And also called Upaghātakakamma. See also - Upaghātaka-(1). (Ti) (2) Approaches and destroys.
upacchedakakamma: [Upacchedaka+kamma] (na) CL=7 An action that approaches and destroys. Upacchedakakamma. That is also called Upaghātakakamma. See also - Upaghātaka-(1).
upacchedana: [Upa+chida+yu] (na) CL=7 (1) Cutting off. (2) A dhamma or nature that is a cause of cutting off.
upacchedīyati: [Upa+chida+ya+te] (kamma,kri) CL=7 Should be cut off. See - Upacchedana.
upacchijjamāna: [Upa+chida+ya+māna] (ti) CL=7 Cut off or broke. See - Upacchijjamānasantāna.
upacchijjamānasantāna: [Upacchijjamāna+santāna]  CL=9 Having the broken- annihilated continuity-  series of aggregates; one.

upacchijji: [Upa+chida+ya+ī] (kri) CL=7 Cut off or completely stopped. See - Upacchijjati.

upacchijjissati: [Upa+chida+ya+ssati] (kri) CL=7 (Someone) will be cut off. See - Upacchijjati.

upacchindi: [Upa+chida+ī] (kri) CL=7 He broke off. See - Upacchindati.
upacchindissati: [Upa+chida+ssati] (kri) CL=7 He will cut. See - Upacchindati.
upacchinna: [Upa+chida+ta] (ti) CL=7 (1) Should be cut off. (2) Cut off. Terminated. Completely stopped. Stopped and finished.
upacchinnaassāsapassāsasañcāra: [Upacchinna+assāsapassāsasañcāra] (ti) CL=7 Circles in and out breathing that are cut off. One who cut off the circle of in and out breathing.
upacchinnadvāravaḷañja: [Upacchinna+dvāravaḷañja] (ti) CL=7 Cut off using the three body"s doors. One who doesn"t use the three body"s doors.
upacchinnakhuddakapalibodha: [Upacchinna+khuddakapalibodha] (ti) CL=7 With a small obstruction that is cut off. One who cut off a small obstruction.
upacchinnapakkha: [Upacchinna+pakkha] (ti) CL=7 One who cuts off his associations.
upacchinnapalibodha: [Upacchinna+palibodha] (ti) CL=7 One who has cut off a small obstruction.
upacchinnasantāna: [Upacchinna+santāna] (ti) CL=7 One who has broken continuums.
upacchinnasaṃyojana: [Upacchinna+saṃyojana] (ti) CL=7 One who has a chain or bond that has cut off.

upacchādemi: [Upa+chada+ṇe+mi] (kri) CL=7 Covers or conceals. See - Upacchādeti.
upacciṃsu: [U+paca+ya+uṃ] (kri) CL=7 They are ripe and red.
upacela: [Yādicchakanāma] (pu) CL=7 A universal monarch is named Upacela(upaceḷa). (A universal monarch who is a future Venerable Nanda, a younger brother of Lord Buddha).
upaceḷa: [Yādicchakanāma] (pu) CL=7 A universal monarch is named Upacela(upaceḷa). (A universal monarch who is a future Venerable Nanda, a younger brother of Lord Buddha).
upacikakkhāyika: [Upacikā+khāyika] (ti) CL=7 (The cloth) white ants bite that.
upacikakkhāyita: [Upacākā+khāyika] (ti) CL=7 (The cloth) white ants bite that.
upacikarāji: [Upacikā+rāji] (thī) CL=7 The line of white ants they are going in a row.
upacikākhāyita: [Upacikā+khāyita] (ti) CL=7 (Paṃsūkū cloth) white ants bite that.
upacikāmocanattha: [Upacikā+mocanattha] (pu) CL=7 Benefits of being free from the harm of white ants.
upacikāsaṅkā: [Upacikā+āsaṅkā] (thī) CL=7 Misconceptions about white ants. There is doubt that the white ants may be bitten or not.
upacinanta: [Upa+ci+nā+anta.thī-] (ti) CL=7 [Upacinantī] One who is striving and heaping up.
upacinanti: [Upa+ci+nā+anti]  CL=9 (They) practice and develop- cause to accumulate. See - Upacinati.
upacinati: [Upa+ci+nā+ti] (kri) CL=7 Acquires. Strives or practices. Causes to heap up. Causes to happen.
upacineyya: [Upa+ci+nā+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should acquire, strive, and heap up. See - Upacinati.
[Upa+ci+nā+eyyaṃ] (kri) CL=7 He should acquire, practice, and accumulate. See - Upacinati.
upacineyyaṃ: [Upa+ci+nā+eyyaṃ] (kri) CL=7 He should acquire, practice, and accumulate. See - Upacinati.
upacini: [Upa+ci+nā+ī] (kri) CL=7 He acquired, practiced, and accumulated. See - Upacinati.
upacinitabba: [Upa+ci+nā+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be lined up or heaped up.
upacinitvā: [Upa+ci+nā+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (A) Having acquired. Having practiced. Having accumulated. Having caused to happen. (B) Having gathered up in all directions. Having heaped up the firewood.
upacinoti: [Upa+ci+ṇu+ti] (kri) CL=7 [Ṇa-kārassa nakārattaṃ. Nīti,dhātu. 245. Rū. 512.] Acquires. Causes to accumulate. Cause to fulfill.
upacintā: [Upa+citi(cinta)+a+ā]  CL=9 Thinking about the cause-method- way.
upacināti: [Upa+ci+nā+ti] (kri) CL=7 He acquires. He practices. He causes to accumulate. He causes to happen.
upacita: [Upa+ci+ta] (ti) CL=7 (1) Should be acquired repeatedly. (2) That is the beginning. Increased in the past. (The form) that is being.
upacitacetanā: [Upacitā+cetanā] (thī) CL=7 Having the intention that is to acquire.
upacitadosa: [Upacita+dosa] (ti) CL=7 A flaw or ill-will that is increased.
upacitakammābhāva: [Upacitakamma+abhāva] (pu) CL=7 Lack of an action that is acquiring, practicing, and accumulation.
upacitakusala: [Upacita+kusala] (ti) CL=7 One who has merits that has acquired.
upacitakusaladhamma: [Upacita+kusaladhamma] (ti) CL=7 One who has wholesome deeds that have been acquired.
upacitamahaggatakamma: [Upacita+mahaggatakamma] (ti) CL=7 One who strives Mahaggata kamma.
upacitamanaka: [Upacita+mana+ka] (ti) CL=7 One who has an acquired mind. One who has a strong and eager mind (such as to do wholesome deeds).
upacitamānasa: [Upacita+mānasa] (ti) CL=7 One who has an acquired mind. One who has a strong and eager mind (such as to do wholesome deeds).
upacitapuñña: [Upacita+puñña] (ti) CL=7 One who has merits that have been acquired. One who has a lot of wholesome deeds.
upacitapuññasambhāra: [Upacita+puññasambhāra] (ti) CL=7 One who has accumulated merits that have been acquired.
upacitapuññasañcaya: [Upacita+puññasañcaya] (ti) CL=7 One who has accumulated wholesome deeds that have been acquired.
upacitapāpakamma: [Upacita+pāpakamma] (ti) CL=7 One who has accumulated unwholesome deeds that have been acquired.
upacitarūpapadaṭṭhāna: [Upacita+rūpa+padaṭṭhāna]  CL=9 Having the proximate cause, which is the original form- the developing form- the aring form.
upacitasambhāra: [Upacita+sambhāra] (ti) CL=7 One who has accumulated merits that have been acquired.
upacitatanutambaloma: [Upacita+tanutambaloma] (ti) CL=7 One who has small and red hair that is in a row.
upacitatta: [Upacita+tta] (na) CL=7 As the state of one who practices repeatedly to accumulate.
upacitavimokkhasambhāra: [Upacita+vimokkhasambhāra] (ti) CL=7 One who has accumulated merits that have been acquired.
upacitavipulapuññasambhāra: [Upacita+vipulapuññasambhāra] (ti) CL=7 One who has accumulated merits that have been acquired.
upacitānavajjakamma: [Upacita+anavajjakamma] (ti) CL=7 One who has wholesome deeds that have been acquired.
upaciyati: [Upa+ci+ya+te] (kamma,kri) CL=7 He is heaped up or He practices and causes to heap up.
upaciṇṇa: [Upa+cara+ta] (na) CL=7 The path that should be practiced.
upacālā: [Upa+cāla] (thī) CL=7 One who is named Upacālā. There are four persons who are named Upacālā in Sāsanā. See original.
upacālī: [Upa+cālī] (thī) CL=7 A novice who is named Upacālī. A novice is named Upacālī who is the son of Upacālā who is a sister of Venerable Sāriputtarā and Venerable Cunda. See - Upacālā-(D).

upacārabhūmi: [Upacāra+bhūmi] (thī) CL=7 (1) The place of vicinity. A moment of preliminary action of stability of mind. (2) The realm of arising a thought where Upacārajhāna arises. A set of Cetasika dhamma that is yoking with Upacārajhāna.
upacāragata: [Upacāra+gata] (ti) CL=7 One who is inside a place that is 18 feet long.
upacārajjhāna: [Upacāra+jhāna] (na) CL=7 Upacārajjhāna. (A) A Jhāna that arises near appanājhāna. (B) Upacārajjhāna that is the proximate cause of Magga. (The upacārajjhāna has ten factors except from Kāyagatāsati, ānāpānassati that are eight factors of Anussati, Āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, and catudhātuvavatthāna).
upacārajjhānacitta: [Upacārajjhāna+citta] (na) CL=7 The mind of the vicinity of the stage of meditation.

upacārajjhānapuñña: [Upacārajjhāna+puñña] (na) CL=7 The virtue that is Upacārajjhāna.
upacārajjhānasampayuttacittuppāda: [Upacārajjhānasampayutta+cittuppāda] (pu) CL=7 A set of intentions that are yoking with Upacārajjhāna.
upacārajjhānasannissaya: [Upacārajjhāna+sannissaya] (pu) CL=7 The dependent dhamma that is Upacārajjhāna.
upacārajjhānādhigama: [Upacārajjhana+adhigama] (pu) CL=7 A period of attainment of Upacārajhāna.
upacārajjhānāropana: [Upacārajjhāna+āropana] (na) CL=7 Rising up to attain Upacārajhāna.
upacārakammakaraṇa: [Upacāra+kamma+karaṇa] (na) CL=7 Doing the function or action that should be done and is in the vicinity.
upacārakammaṭṭhāna: [Upacāra+āvaha+kammaṭṭhāna] (na) CL=7 Upacārakammaṭṭhāna. Kammaṭṭhāna that brings to attain Upacārajhāna.
upacāramattalābhī: [Upacāramatta+lābhī] (ti) CL=7 One who gets merely Upacārajhāna.
upacāramattasiddha: [Upacāramatta+siddha]  CL=9 Completed with just the metaphorical calling- expression.
upacāraniddesa: [Upacāra+niddesa] (pu) CL=7 Analytical description by a simile or metaphor.
upacāraniyama: [Upacāra+niyama] (pu) CL=7 Demarcates the vicinity place or surrounding area.
upacāraniyamanattha: [Upacāra+niyamana+attha] (pu) CL=7 Benefits of demarcation of the surrounding area.
upacārapatta: [Upacāra+patta] (ti) CL=7 Attained the state of Upacārabhāvanā.
upacārapaññā: [Upacāra+paññā] (thī) CL=7 Upacārapaññā. The wisdom that arises in the vicinity of appanā wisdom.
upacārappanābheda: [Upacārappanā+bheda] (pu) CL=7 (1) There is a variety that are upacāra and appanā. (Ti) (2) There are a variety of (samādhi, Jhāna) that are upacāra, appanā.
upacārappanākkhaṇa: [Upacārappanā+khaṇa] (pu) CL=7 A moment of arising of upacārabhāvanā, appanābhāvanā.
upacārappanāsamādhi: [Upacārappanā+āvaha] (pu) CL=7 Brings to attain upacārajhāna, appanājhāna.
upacārappanāsamādhirahita: [Upacārappanā+samādhi] (ti) CL=7 Access concentration and absorption concentration.
upacārappanāsamādhivirahita: [Upacārappanāsamādhi+rahita] (ti) CL=7 Free from access concentration and absorption concentration.

upacārappatti: [Upacāra+patti] (thī) CL=7 Reaches or attains upacāra bhāvanā.
upacārarūpajjhānasamādhi: [Upacāra+rūpajjhāna+samādhi] (pu) CL=7 Access concentration and stability of rūpajhāna.

upacārasaññā: [Upacāra+saññā] (thī) CL=7 The perception of upacāra jhāna.

upalabbhanti: [Upa+labha+ya+ante]  CL=9 (Ante is reversed into anti.) That should be attained. That should be known by approaching with wisdom. See - Upalabbhati.
upalabbhanīya: [Upa+labha+ya+anīya]  CL=9 That sould be attained. Should be known by approaching with wisdom.
upalabbhati: [Upa+labha+ya+te]  CL=9 That should be attained, that should be known by approaching with wisdom.
upalabbheyya: [Upa+labha+ya+etha] (kamma,kri) CL=7 He should know or have insight by approaching with wisdom. See - Upalabbhati.
upalabbheyyuṃ: [Upa+labha+ya+eraṃ] (kamma,kri) CL=7 They should know or have insight by approaching with wisdom. See - Upalabbhati.
upalabbhitabba: [Upa+labha+ya+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be attained. Should be known or insight by approaching with wisdom.
upalabbhiyamāna: [Upa+labha+ya+māna] (ti) CL=7 Should be known or insight by approaching with wisdom.
upalabhanti: [Upa+labha+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They acquire or get or attain. They know. See - Upalabhati.
upalabhati: [Upa+labha+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He gets or attains. He knows.
upalabhi: [Upa+labha+ī] (kri) CL=7 He got or attained. He knew. See - Upalabhati.
upalabhiṃsu: [Upa+labha+ñaṃ] (kri) CL=7 They got or attained. They knew. See - Upalabhati.
upalabhāma: [Upa+labha+a+ma] (kri) CL=7 We get or attain. We know. See - Upalabhati.
upaladdha: [Upa+labha+ta] (ti) CL=7 Acquired or attained or got. Knew or insight.
upaladdhabba: [Upa+labha+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Worthy to get or attain.
upaladdhadhamma: [Upaladdha+dhamma]  CL=9 The nature that is obtained- known.
upaladdhapubba: [Upaladdha+pubba] (ti) CL=7 Got or attained in the past.
upaladdhapubbasaṅketa: [Upaladdhapubba+saṅketa] (ti) CL=7 With the sign that attained or got in the past.
upaladdhasabhāva: [Upaladdha+sabhāva] (pu) CL=7 The characteristics that should be acquired or got.
upaladdhi: [Upa+labha+ti] (thī) CL=7 (1) Getting or attaining. The nature of taking or accepting. (2) The belief. Assuming. Opinion or view. Deep-seated feeling or belief. (3) The nature of being obviously.
upaladdhihetu: [Upaladdhi+hetu] (pu) CL=7 A cause of getting or conception.
upaladdhinissitakathā: [Upaladdhi+nissitakathā] (thī) CL=7 Words (sound) that are based on the conception of 'living beings'.
upaladdhiokāsa: [Upaladdhi+okāsa] (pu) CL=7 The place of getting. (If concentrated by the wisdom, that is the place of getting a person or conception).
upaladdhisāmañña: [Upaladdhi+sāmañña]  CL=7 A state of agreement or similarity based on understanding or view. (If someone focuses and contemplates with wisdom, meditating on the nature of experience, and aligns their perspective with that which can be attained, it leads to a state of similarity or accord characterized by understanding or conception).
upaladdhisāmaññapucchā: [Upaladdhisāmañña+pucchā]  CL=9 The question that asks about the state of being the same in terms of availablity. See Upaladdhisāmañña.
upalakkhaye: [Upa+lakkha+ṇaya+eyya] (kri) CL=7 Should make a mental note or bear in mind. See - Upalakkhayati.
upalakkhayitvā: [Upa+lakkha+ṇaya+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having made a mental note.
upalakkhayitvāna: [Upa+lakkha+ṇaya+tvāna] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having made a mental note.
upalakkhaṇa: [Upa+lakkha+yu] (thī,na) CL=7 (A) (The wisdom) that is the nature of concentration and contemplation (the sign of anicca, etc.,). (B) The words (sound) that are a cause of memorizing or recognition. The mark or sign that is a cause of memorizing or recognition. Upalakkhaṇa method. (memorizing or recognizing the fraction and the collection that way is called Upalakkhaṇa. Pudacaca. 205). (C) Meditation. Concentration and contemplation. (D) A cause of concentration and contemplation.
upalakkhaṇakāraṇa: [Upalakkhaṇa+kāraṇa] (na) CL=7 The sign of concentration and contemplation.
upalakkhaṇanaya: [Upalakkhaṇa+naya] (pu) CL=7 Upalakkhaṇanaya or the discrimination method. The way that shows a part and also takes a collection.
upalakkhaṇapada: [Upalakkhaṇa+pada] (na) CL=7 The words that teach the discrimination. The words that teach the upalakkhaṇa method.
upalakkhaṇavacana: [Upalakkhaṇa+vacana] (na) CL=7 The statement or words (sound) that explain the discrimination.
upalakkhaṇākāra: [Upalakkhaṇa+ākāra] (ti) CL=7 The manner or state of affairs that approaches and recognizes the sense.
upalakkhaṇīya: [Upa+lakkha+anīya]  CL=9 Should be noted. See -  Upalakkhaṇīyasabhāva.
upalakkhaṇīyasabhāva: [Upalakkhaṇīya+sabhāva] (ti) CL=7 The nature of discrimination or making a mental note.
upalakkhesiṃ: [Upa+lakkha+ṇe+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 Made a mental note or discrimination. See - Upalakkheti.
upalakkhetabba: [Upa+lakkha+ṇe+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be concentrated and contemplated.
upalakkhetabbākāra: [Upalakkhetabba+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner or state affairs of concentration and contemplation.
upalakkheti: [Upa+lakkha+ṇe+ti] (kri) CL=7 Keep in mind. Make a mental note. Approach and discriminate.
upalakkhetuṃ: [Upa+lakkha+ṇe+tuṃ] (bya) CL=7 To make a mental note or to concentrate and contemplate.
upalakkhetvā: [Upa+lakkha+ṇe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having made a mental note or having concentrated and contemplated.
upalakkheyya: [Upa+lakkha+ṇe+eyya] (kri) CL=7 Should make a mental note or should concentrate and contemplate. See - Upalakkheti.
upalakkhita: [Upa+lakkha+ta] (ti) CL=7 Made a mental note or concentrated and contemplated.
upalakkhitabba: [Upa+lakkha+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be made a mental note or should be concentrated and contemplated.
upalakkhitasamādhānākāra: [Upalakkhita+samādhānākāra] (ti) CL=7 The state of affairs of mindfulness that is concentrated and contemplated.
upalakkhīyanti: [Upa+lakkha+ya+ante] (kamma,kri) CL=7 They concentrate and contemplate. See - Upalakkhīyati.
upalavati: [U+palava+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 [Dhātvattha. 225.] Fly up. Fly into the sky.
upalavitvā: [U+palava+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Emerges or appears on the surface of the water.
upalaḷa: [Upa+laḷa+a+hi] (kri) CL=7 May you dwell. May you have fun. May you play. See - Upalaḷati.
upalepa: [Upa+lipa+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 Applying or smearing. See - Upalepabhaya.
upalepabhaya: [Upalepa+bhaya] (na) CL=7 Fear of contamination or applying or smearing.
upalikkhanti: [Upa+likha+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They shot and cut. See - Upalikkhati.
upalimpanti: [Upa+lipa+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They smear. They apply. They cotaminate. They stick (to). See - Upalimpati.
upalimpare: [Upa+lipa+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They smear. They apply. They cotaminate. They stick (to). See - Upalimpati.
upalimpati: [Upa+lipa+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 [Nīti, dhā. 216.] He smears. He applies. He contaminates. He sticks (to).
upalippati: [Upa+lipa+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 [See - Lippati]. He is smeared or he is defiled. (Nopalippati=nupalippati= is not smeared, is not contanimated).
upalippāmi: [Upa+lipa+a+mi] (kri) CL=7 Smears or contaminates. See - Upalippati.
upallavati: [U+palava+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 Transform or change or move.
upallaviṃ: [U+pala+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 The transition has taken place. Upallavati - Look.
upalliṇḍupoṭṭalaka: [Upalliṇḍu+poṭṭalaka] (na) CL=7 The house or nest of the insect is called Upalliṇḍu.
upalobhetvā: [Upa+lubha+ṇe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having caused confusion. Having persuaded.
upalālenta: [Upa+lala+ṇe+anta] (ti) CL=7 [Dhātvattha. 336. In Thī upalālentī] One who pacifies (someone) tenderly.
upalālentī: [Upa+lala+ṇe+anta+ī] (thī) CL=7 One who pacifies (someone) tenderly. See - Upalālenta.
upalāpaka: [Upa+lapa+ṇvu] (ti) CL=7 [Nīti, dhā. 323.] One who flatters by gracious speaking.
upalāpanattha: [Upalāpana+attha] (pu) CL=7 The benefits of causing persuasion.
upalāpenta: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+anta] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī upalāpentī] One who persuades.
upalāpentī: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+anta+ī] (thī) CL=7 One who persuades. See - Upalāpenta.
upalāpessanti: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+ssanti] (kri) CL=7 They will persuade. See - Upalāpeti.
upalāpessatha: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+ssatha] (kri) CL=7 You (pl) will persuade. See - Upalāpeti.
upalāpetabba: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+tabba] (ti) CL=7 One who should be spoken kindly. (Should persuade by gracious speaking (words). Sya).
upalāpeti: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+ti] (kri) CL=7 [Nīti, dhā. 323] He persuades. He induces. He coaxes. He talks kindly. He flatters. He appeases or soothes.
upalāpetuṃ: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+tuṃ] (bya) CL=7 To persuade. To cause dissension (among friends).
upalāpetvā: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (1) Having persuaded. Having induced. Having coaxed. (2) Having made the sound repeat again and again. Having blown.
upalāpeyya: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should persuade. See - Upalāpeti.
upalāpeyyuṃ: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+eyyuṃ] (kri) CL=7 They should persuade. See - Upalāpeti.
upalāpeyyāma: [Upa+lapa+ṇe+eyyāma] (kri) CL=7 We should persuade. See - Upalāpeti.
upalāḷayamāna: [Upa+ghaḷa+ṇaya+māna] (ti) CL=7 One who causes to rejoice.
upalāḷenta: [Upa+laḷa+ṇe+anta] (ti) CL=7 (1) One who causes to rejoice. (2) One who makes ornaments and to be graceful.
upalīyana: [Upa+lī+ya+yu]  CL=9 (1) The place where one approaches and takes shelter- hides. hiding place. (2) Taking shelter and hiding after approaching.
upalīyanādhippāya: [Upalīyana+adhippāya] (pu) CL=7 The desire to approach and hide.
upamatta: [Upamā+tta] (na) CL=7 As a simile or a state of a simile.
upamattaya: [Upamā+taya] (na) CL=7 The sum of the three similes.
upamattha: [Upamā+attha] (pu) CL=7 (1) The meaning of a simile. (Ti) (2) With the meaning of a simile.
upamaññagotta: [Upamañña+gotta] (ti) CL=7 One who is an upamañña lineage.
upamenta: [Upa+mā+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who desires to compare or make a simile.
upameti: [Upa+mā+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He compares. He makes a simile.
upametvā: [Upa+mā+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having compared. Having made a simile.
upameyya: [Upa+mā+ṇya] (ti) CL=7 [Upamīyatīti upameyyaṃ. Alaṅkā, ṭī. 176-gāthā. Upecca minituṃ arahatīti upameyyaṃ. Nirutti, nhā. 533.] Thing or object that should be compared.
upameyyadassana: [Upameyya+pakkha] (na) CL=7 The words that show the compared thing or object.
upameyyapakkha: [Upameyya+pakkha] (pu) CL=7 The side of the comparison or a simile.
upameyyasampaṭipādanattha: [Upameyya+sampaṭipādanattha] (pu) CL=7 The benefit of the application of a simile is that is complete and obvious.
upameyyattha: [Upameyya+attha] (pu) CL=7 (An object or thing) of a meaning that is compared or makes a simile.
upameyyatthadassana: [Upameyyattha+dassana] (na) CL=7 Words (sound) that show a comparable meaning.
upameyyatthadīpanī: [Upameyyattha+dīpanī] (thī) CL=7 Explanatory work for the comparable meaning.
upameyyatthavibhāvanattha: [Upameyyattha+vibhāvanattha] (ti) CL=7 The benefit that explains clearly the comparable meaning.
upameyyatthānurūpa: [Upameyyattha+anurūpa] (ti) CL=7 In accordance with the comparable meaning.
upameyyavāra: [Upameyya+vāra]  CL=9 The turn/time of the person being compared; the turn/time of the talk of what is being compared.
upameyyopamādassanamukha: [Upameyyopamā+dassanamuda] (na) CL=7 Making first and foremost an explanation of the comparable object or thing.
upamita: [Upa+mā+ta] (ti) CL=7 Compared or should be compared.
upamitabba: [Upa+mā+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be compared. Should be made a simile.
upamitapuggala: [Upamita+puggala] (pu) CL=7 A person who should be compared.
upamitauposatha: [Upamita+uposatha] (pu) CL=7  'Uposatha day' or observance day ceremonies that should be compared.
upamiya: [Upa+mā+ṇya] (ti) CL=7 Compared or should be compared.
upamopameyya: [Upamā+upameyya] (na) CL=7 A simile. A subject of comparison.
upamopameyyasaṃsandananaya: [Upamopameyya+saṃsandananaya] (pu) CL=7 The way that discusses a simile and a subject of comparison.
upamopameyyasāmañña: [Upamopameyya+sāmañña] (na) CL=7 As the state of similarity of a simile and subject of comparison.
upamopamitabba: [Upamā+upamitabba] (ti) CL=7 The object or thing that should be compared which is a simile and a subject of comparison.
upamopamitabbasambandha: [Upamopamitabba+sambandha] (pu) CL=7 The connection of a simile and subject of comparison.
upamopamitabbasarūpa: [Upamopamitabba+sarūpa] (na) CL=7 The same form of a simile and subject of comparison.
upamā: [Upa+mā+a] (thī) CL=7 The nature of similarity. Similarity to a simile and subject of comparison. (Lord Buddha"s face is like a Padummā lotus, in these words, Lord Buddha"s face and Padummā lotus are graceful and are similar to what status is called a simile).
upamābhindana: [Upamā+bhindana] (na) CL=7 Deleting or breaking up a simile.
upamājotaka: [Upamā+jotaka] (ti) CL=7 Points out the meaning of a simile.
upamākathana: [Upamā+kathana] (na) CL=7 Teaches or preaches a simile.
upamākāra: [Upamā+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The state of affairs of comparison. The state of similarity.
upamākāranigamanattha: [Upamākāra+nigamanattha]  CL=9 Having sth that concludes upamākāra. See upamākāra.
upamāmukha: [Upamā+mukha] (na) CL=7 Makes first and foremost a simile.
upamāna: [Upa+mā+yu] (na) CL=7 [Upamīyati etenāti upamānaṃ. Rū. 536. Moga, pañcikā, 5-kaṇḍa, 6-sutta. Upa+māna. Ma, ṭī, 1. 268.] The object or thing that is a cause of comparison. Thing or object that arises near the comparison.
upamānabhāva: [Upamāna+bhāva] (pu) CL=7 As a simile. As a state of a comparison object or thing.
upamānadhammakathā: [Upamāna+dhammakathā] (thī) CL=7 Words (sound) that explain a simile or discussion of the nature of a thing with a simile.
upamānapubbapada: [Upamāna+pubbapada]  CL=7 A relative compound (bahubbīhi samāsa) in which the comparison word (upamāna) is placed as the first element is called an upamānapubbapada bahubbīhi samāsa.
upamānuttarapada: [Upamāna+uttarapada] (ti) CL=7 A comparison word that is at behind, A comparison word that should be placed at behind (Kammadhārayasamāsa).
upamānākāra: [Upamāna+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The state of affairs of comparison. The state of similarity.
upamāpamāṇa: [Upamā+pamāṇa] (na) CL=7 The extent that is a simile.
upamāpañha: [Upamā+pañha] (ti) CL=7 A question that should be explained with a simile. A question of a simile.
upamāpubbaka: [Upamā+pubbaka] (ti) CL=7 With a simile in the past. Has a former simile.
upamārahita: [Upamā+rahita] (ti) CL=7 Free from a simile. (Buddha) who is without comparison.
upamārahitasarīra: [Upamārahita+sarīra] (ti) CL=7 (Buddha) whose body is without comparison.
upamāsampādana: [Upamā+sampādana] (na) CL=7 Shows and discusses a simile and subject of comparison.
upamāsaṃsandana: [Upamā+saṃsandana] (na) CL=7 Shows and discusses a simile and subject of comparison.
upamāsaṃsandanavacana: [Umapāsaṃsandana+vacana] (na) CL=7 Words (sound) that explain the discussion of a simile and subject of comparison.
upamātaddhita: [Upamā+taddhita] (pu,na) CL=7 Iva, viyasaddā kyeso taddhita that preaches or teaches the meaning of a simile.
upamāttaya: [Upamā+taya] (na) CL=7 A collection of three similes.
upamātu: [Upa+mātu] (thī) CL=7 A guardian. A wet-nurse. (One who takes care of others" children like a mother).
upamāvacana: [Upamā+vacana] (na) CL=7 The word that teaches the meaning of a simile.
upamāvatthu: [Upamā+vatthu] (na) CL=7 An object that is a cause of comparison.
upamāvāra: [Upamā+vāra]  CL=9 The turn/time of the talk of the (majjhima, dahara) persons with whom sth is being compared.
upamūpameyyadvaya: [Upama] (na) CL=7 [Upameyya+dvaya] The sum of a simile and subject of comparison.
upamūpameyyasambandha: [Upamūpameyya+sambandha] (pu) CL=7 Connection with a simile and subject of comparison.
upamūpameyyavibhāga: [Upamūpameyya+vibhāga] (pu) CL=7 Analytical description of a simile and subject of comparison.
upanaccanta: [Upa+naccanta] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī upanaccantī] One who dances.
upanaccantī: [Upanaccanta+ī] (thī) CL=7 A woman who is a dancer. A professional dancer. See - Upanaccanta.
upanadanti: [Upa+nada+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They shout loudly or they sing sweetly. See - Upanadati.
upanadati: [Upa+nada+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 Shouts loudly or sings sweetly.
upanaddha: [Ṇaka+naha+ta] (ti) CL=7 Bore enmity towards. One who causes to be angry repeatedly in his mind.
upanahana: [Upa+naha+yu] (na) CL=7 Approaches and binds. Bear enmity towards or grudge. See - Upanahanasīla.
upanahanasīla: [Upanahana+sīla] (ti) CL=7 Used to approach and bind. One who used to bear enmity towards or grudge. See also - Upanayhanasīla.
upanamanta: [Upa+namanta] (ti) CL=7 One who takes refuge in or reveres.
upananda: [Yādicchakanāma] (pu) CL=7 One who is named Upananda. (In Sāsanā, there are six persons who are named Sāsanā. (A) A thera is named Sāsanā who becomes a bhikkhu and comes from Sākīvaṅa king lineage. A thera is interested in begs (for things) and is without dignity. But who is a good preacher or teacher.
upanandasakyaputta: [Upananda+sakyaputta] (pu) CL=7 A thera is named Upananda who is a Sākīvaṅa prince (before becoming a bhikkhu).
upanandatthera: [Upananda+thera] (pu) CL=7 A thera is named Upananda. (who is no.1 A thera is named Upananda).
upanandavatthu: [Upananda+vatthu] (na) CL=7 The story of a thera is named Upananda. (Who is no.1 Upananda).
upanandha: [Upa+nanda+a] (ti) CL=7 Bore enmity towards. One who causes to be angry repeatedly in his mind.
upanandhana: [Upa+nanda+yu] (na) CL=7 Binding or attaching. Binding after layer and layer. Making a tangle or bearing a grudge.
upanandhanalakkhaṇa: [Upanandhana+lakkhaṇa] (ti) CL=7 The sign of making a grudge with anger.
upanandhanasīla: [Upanandhana+sīla] (ti) CL=7 One who used to bear a grudge.
upanandhati: [Upa+nandha+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 [In Dhātvattha. 210. Pācita, yo, Nahadhātu].  Bears enmity towards or grudge.
upanandhiṃsu: [Upa+nandha+uṃ] (kri) CL=7 They bore enmity towards (someone). See - Upanandhati.
upanaya: [Upa+nī+a] (pu) CL=7 (1) Approaches and takes. Causes to arise. (2) The way that should be approached and taken.
upanayamāna: [Upa+nī+a+māna] (ti) CL=7 One who brings or carries.
upanayana: [Upa+nī+yu] (na) CL=7 Approaches and brings. Bring near. Causes to arise.
upanayanacatukka: [Upanayana+catukka] (na) CL=7 The sum of four Upanayana. The four factors that should be memorized by approaching and bringing.
upanayanakicca: [Upanayana+kicca] (ti) CL=7 The function of approaching and bringing.
upanayanapaññatti: [Upanayana+paññatti]  CL=7 The explanation or designation of the opposite cause through bringing it near or applying it in various ways, or the illustration of the opposite cause.
upanayanarasa: [Upanayana+rasa] (ti) CL=7 The function of bringing near to (you).
upanayanasampattika: [Upanayana+sampattika] (ti) CL=7 The perfected quality that is bringing near. See - Upanayanakicca.
upanayanākāra: [Upanayana+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner of bringing near.
upanayaparipākalakkhaṇa: [Upanayaparipāka+lakkhaṇa] (ti) CL=7 The sign that is bringing near to you and has the mature sign.
upanayasi: [Upa+nī+a+si] (kri) CL=7 Brings near. Causes to reach. See - Upanayati-(A).
upanayati: [Upa+nī+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 (A) Brings near. Causes to reach. (B) Offers respectfully. Gives away in charity.
upanayhana: [Upa+naha+ya+yu] (thī,na) CL=7 (A) Binds with anger. The Āghāta object binds the mind. The manner of bearing enmity towards. Bears grudge. (B) Binding or attaching. A cause of binding.
upanayhanakusagga: [Upanayhana+kusagga] (na) CL=7 The Kusa grass that is a cause of binding or wrapping.
upanayhanalakkhaṇa: [Upanayhana+lakkhaṇa] (ti) CL=7 The sign of bearing enmity.
upanayhanasīla: [Upanayhana+sīla] (ti) CL=7 One who used to bear enmity.
upanayhanti: [Upa+naha+ya+anti] (kri) CL=7 They wrap up. They bind. They bear enmity. See - Upanayhati.
upanayhanākāra: [Upanayhana+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner of bearing enmity. See - Upanayhanasīla.
upanayhati: [Upa+naha+ya+ti] (kri) CL=7 He forms. he binds. He wraps up. He packs up. He bears enmity. He grudges.
upanayhita: [Upa+naha+ya+ta] (ti) CL=7 Wraps up with anger. The Āghāta object binds the mind. One who bears enmity. See also - Upanayhanā.
upanayāmase: [Upa+nī+a+āmase] (kri) CL=7 They will bring near. They will cause to reach. They will cause to obey. See - Upanayati-(A).
upanayāmi: [Upa+nī+a+mi] (kri) CL=7 Offers respectfully. Gives away in charity. See - Upanayati-(B).
upanayāpenta: [Upa+nī+ṇāpe+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who causes to bring.
upanehi: [Upa+nī+a+hi] (kri) CL=7 May you bring near. See - Upaneti.
upanema: [Upa+nī+a+ma] (kri) CL=7 We bring near. We offer respectfully. See - Upaneti.
upanemisa: [Yādicchakanāma] (pu) CL=7 A private Buddha is named Upanemisa.
upanenta: [Upa+nī+anta] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī upanentī] One who brings (something) and offers respectfully.
upanenti: [Upa+nī+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They bring near. They offer respectfully. See - Upaneti.
upanentu: [Upa+nī+a+antu] (kri) CL=7 May they bring near. See - Upaneti.
upanentī: [Upa+nī+anta+itthijotaī] (thī) CL=7 A woman who brings and offers respectfully. See - Upanenta.
upanesi: [Upa+nī+ī] (kri) CL=7 He brought near. He offered. See - Upaneti.
[Upa+nī+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 I brought (something) near. I offered. See - Upaneti.
upanesiṃ: [Upa+nī+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 I brought (something) near. I offered. See - Upaneti.
upanessati: [Upa+nī+ssati] (kri) CL=7 He will bring near. See - Upaneti.
upanesuṃ: [Upa+nī+uṃ] (kri) CL=7 They brought near. See - Upaneti.
upanetabba: [Upa+nī+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be brought. Should be filled up. Should be compared.
upanetabbavacana: [Upanetabba+vacana] (na) CL=7 Worthy to talk the complementary words (sound).
upanetabbayuttaka: [Upanetabba+yuttaka] (ti) CL=7 Should bring near and suitable to use.
upanetabbābhāva: [Upanetabba+abhāva] (ti) CL=7 Lack of the complementary words (sound).
upanetha: [Upa+nī+a+tha] (kri) CL=7 May you (pl) approach and listen. See - Upaneti.
upaneti: [Upa+nī+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He brings near. He offers respectfully.
upanetu: [Upa+nī+tu] (ti) CL=7 He brings near. Upanetu(kri) [upa+nī+tu] May he bring near. May he carry (to). May he reach. See - Upaneti.
upanetvā: [Upa+nī+anta] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī upanentī] Having brought and offered respectfully.
upaneyyuṃ: [Upa+nī+eyyuṃ] (kri) CL=7 They should bring near. They should offer. See - Upaneti.
upanibaddha: [Upa+ni+badha(bandha)+ta]  CL=7 (A) One who is bound or attached. (B) That which should be arranged and created. (C) That which should be in.
upanibaddhakukkura: [Upanibaddha+kukkura] (pu) CL=7 A dog that is tied.
upanibaddhasaññī: [Upanibaddhasaññā+ī] (ti) CL=7 One who has a perception that is always tied.
upanibaddhasunakha: [Upanibaddha+sunakha]  CL=1 A dog that is tied.
upanibajjhate: [Upa+ni+badha+ya+te] (kri) CL=7 Sticks to. ties to. Strongly attached to (someone or something). See - Upanibajjhati.
upanibajjhati: [Upa+ni+badha+ya+ti] (kri) CL=7 Sticks to. Ties to. Strongly attached to (someone or something). Binds up.
upanibandhacitta: [Upanibandha+citta] (na) CL=7 One who has an attached mind.
upanibandhagocara: [Upanibandha+gocara] (pu) CL=7 (The sense) of Kammaṭṭhāna that is a cause of binding the mind.
upanibandhana: [Upa+ni+bandha+yu] (na,thī) CL=7 (1) A grass or creeper vine that is a cause of binding. (2) Binds to close. to make close and bind repeatedly. (Ti) (3) (Mind, mindfulness) that is a cause of approaching and binding. (4) Tied or attached.
upanibandhananimitta: [Upanibandhanā(na)] (na) CL=7 [Nimitta]. The sense of mindfulness that is a cause of binding the mind to the senses. (the tip of the nostril, the upper lip). The sign that is the tip of the nostril where in and out breathing is binding. The sign that is the upper lip where in and out breathing are binding. The sign (of touching in and out breathing) that is bound by the mark of recognition. The tip of the nostril and the upper lip that is the cause of the recognition Assāsapassāsa of mindfulness which is the cause of binding the mind to the sense.
upanibandhananimittasaññita: [Upanibandhanānimitta+saññita] (ti) CL=7 Should bear in mind the sign of mindfulness that is a cause of binding the mind to the sense.
upanibandhanasamattha: [Upanibandhana+samattha] (ti) CL=7 Ability to approach and bind.
upanibandhanathambha: [Upanibandhana+thambha] (pu) CL=7 (1) A pole that is tied. A hitching post or pole. (Ti) (2) (The tip of the nostril, the upper lip) that is like a hitching pole (a pole that is tied). See - Upanibandhanathambhamūla.
upanibandhanathambhamūla: [Upanibandhanatha(ttha)mbha+mūla] (na) CL=7 Near the sign pole that is the tip of the nostril, and the upper lip that is like a hitching pole (a pole that is tied). Near the pole that is the so-called upper lip, and the tip of the nostril is a binding place for in and out breathing. The base of the sign pole that is the tip of the nostril, upper lip that is like the pole tying the cow.
upanibandhanattha: [Upanibandhana+attha] (pu) CL=7 (1) The meaning of being close and tying together. (Ti) (2) The benefit of being close and tied together.
upanibandhanatthambha: [Upanibandhana+thambha] (pu) CL=7 (1) A pole that is tied. A hitching post or pole. (Ti) (2) (The tip of the nostril, the upper lip) that is like a hitching pole (a pole that is tied). See - Upanibandhanathambhamūla.
upanibandhanatthambhamūla: [Upanibandhanatha(ttha)mbha+mūla] (na) CL=7 Near the sign pole that is the tip of the nostril, and the upper lip that is like a hitching pole (a pole that is tied). Near the pole that is the so-called upper lip, the tip of the nostril that is a binding place of in and out breathing. The base of the sign pole that is the tip of the nostril, upper lip that is like the pole tying the cow.
upanibandhanaṭṭha: [Upanibandhana+attha] (pu) CL=7 (1) The meaning of being close and tying together. (Ti) (2) The benefit of being close and tied together.
upanibandhanaṭṭhāna: [Upanibandhana+ṭhāna] (ti) CL=7 A place where (something) is binding close to.
upanibandhanti: [Upa+ni+bandha+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They tie close (to). See - Upanibandhati.
upanibandhanānimitta: [Upanibandhanā(na)] (na) CL=7 [Nimitta]. The sense of mindfulness that is a cause of binding the mind to the senses. (the tip of the nostril, the upper lip). The sign that is the tip of the nostril where in and out breathing is binding. The sign that is the upper lip where in and out breathing are binding. The sign (of touching in and out breathing) that is bound by the mark of recognition. (paṭisaṃ, say). The tip of the nostril and the upper lip that is the cause of the recognition Assāsapassāsa of mindfulness which is the cause of binding the mind to the sense.
upanibandhanānimittasaññita: [Upanibandhanānimitta+saññita] (ti) CL=7 Should bear in mind the sign of mindfulness that is a cause of binding the mind to the sense.
upanibandhanānisaṃsa: [Upanibandhana+ānisaṃsa] (ti) CL=7 The benefit of bringing near and binding together. See - Upanibandhanattha(ti)-(2).
upanibandhasaññī: [Upanibandhasaññā+ī]  CL=9 Having the perception that is always bound. See - Upanibaddhasaññī.
upanibandhati: [Upa+ni+bandha+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He ties close to. He binds together.
upanibandhitvā: [Upa+ni+bandha+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (A) Having tied onto. Having fastened. Having made a mental note in the mind. (B) Having connected. Having communicated. (C) Having written.
upanibandhāhi: [Upa+ni+bandha+a+hi] (kri) CL=7 May you tie close to. See - Upanibandhati.
upanibandhāpesi: [Upa+ni+bandha+ṇāpe+ī] (kā,kri) CL=7 Caused to tie close to. To be consistent in the duty of offering that is always doing. Established the duty of offering forever.
upanibandhāpeti: [Upa+ni+bandha+ṇāpe+ti] (kā,kri) CL=7 Causes to tie close to. To be consistent in the duty of offering that is always doing. Establishes the duty of offering forever.
upanibandhāpetvā: [Upa+ni+bandha+ṇāpe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having caused to tie close to. To be consistent in the duty of offering that is always doing. Having established the duty of offering forever.
upanidhi: [Upa+ni+dhā+i] (pu) CL=7 (1) Deposits of wealth. Compares at the near place. Considers. Sympathy. Comparison. Simile.
upanidhikathā: [Upanidhi+kathā] (thī) CL=7 Words (sound) that teach for the deposits of wealth. A section that teaches about the decision for the offense of stealing the deposits of the wealth.
upanidhā: [Upa+ni+dhā+a+ā(=itthījotaka)] (thī) CL=7 Place near. Comparison. Simile. Consider.
upanidhāpaññatti: [Upanidhā+paññatti]  CL=7 A descriptive or comparative expression, where one thing is considered concerning another, such as thinking of one thing as representing two, two as representing three, a long term as representing a short term, or a short term as representing a long term.
upanidhāya: [Upa+ni+dhā+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (A) To place near. To lean against. To pillow. (To pillow a bone of a corpse). (B) To compare. To consider. To sympathize.
upanighaṃsanta: [Upa+ni+ghasi=(ghaṃsa)] (ti) CL=7 [Anta. In Thī upanighaṃsantī] One who rubs against (something). (kri, vi) Rubbing against.
upanighaṃsantī: [Upa+ni+ghasi=(ghaṃsa)+anta+ī] (thī) CL=7 She rubs against (something). See - Upanighaṃsanta.
upanighaṃsiyamāna: [Upa+ni+ghaṃsa+ya+māna] (ti) CL=7 One who is rubbed against.
upanijjhāna: [Upa+ni+jhe+yu] (na) CL=7 (1) A state of approaching, concentration, and contemplation. Intense concentration and contemplation. (Ti) (2) Intense contemplated.
upanijjhānacitta: [Upanijjhāna+citta] (na) CL=7 The mind that intensely concentrates and contemplates.
upanijjhānakicca: [Upanijjhāna+kicca] (ti) CL=7 The function of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhānalakkhaṇa: [Upanijjhāna+lakkhaṇa] (na) CL=7 (1) The sign of intense concentration and contemplation. (Ti) (2) With the sign of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhānalakkhaṇappatta: [Upanijjhānilakkhaṇa+patta] (ti) CL=7 Reaches a state of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhānākāra: [Upanijjhāna+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner of intense meditation.
upanijjhāya: [Upa+ni+jhe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 To intensely concentrate and contemplate or to intensely meditate.
upanijjhāyanabhāvapaṭilābha: [Upanijjhāyanabhāva+paṭilābha] (na) CL=7 Attain the state of dhamma that intensely concentrates and contemplates. Attain the characteristics of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhāyanabyāpāra: [Upanijjhāyana+byāpāra] (pu) CL=7 The endeavor or diligence that intensely concentrates and contemplates.
upanijjhāyanakicca: [Upanijjhāyana+kicca] (na) CL=7 The function of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhāyanapaccaya: [Upanijjhāyana+paccaya] (pu) CL=7 A cause that intensely concentrates and contemplates.
upanijjhāyanapavatti: [Upanijjhāyana+pavatti] (thī) CL=7 The occurrence of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhāyanasabhāva: [Upanijjhāyana+sabhāva] (pu) CL=7 The nature of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhāyanavatthu: [Upanijjhāyana+vatthu] (na) CL=7 The subject or affairs of intense concentration and contemplation.
upanijjhāyanta: [Upa+ni+jhe+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who intensely concentrates and contemplates.
upanijjhāyanti: [Upa+ni+jhe+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They meditate. They intensely concentrate and contemplate (by natural eyes, wisdom eyes, and Jhānacakkhu). They look intensely (with anger). See - Upanijjhāyati.
upanijjhāyanākāra: [Upanijjhāyana+ākāra] (ti) CL=7 The manner that intensely concentrates and contemplates.
upanijjhāyatha: [Upa+ni+jhe+a+tha] (kri) CL=7 May you (pl) intensely concentrate and contemplate. See - Upanijjhāyati.
upanijjhāyati: [Upa+ni+jhe+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He looks (at). He intensely concentrates and contemplates. He looks intensely (with anger).
upanijjhāyeyya: [Upa+ni+jhe+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should meditate, He should intensely concentrate and contemplate (by normal eyes, wisdom eyes, and Jhānacakkhu). See - Upanijjhāyati.
upanijjhāyi: [Upa+ni+jhe+ī] (kri) CL=7 He meditated. He intensely concentrated and contemplated (by normal eyes, wisdom eyes, and Jhānacakkhu). He looks intensely (with anger). See - Upanijjhāyati.
upanijjhāyimhā: [Upa+ni+jhe+mhā] (kri) CL=7 We intensely looked (at) or they intensely concentrated and contemplated. We intensely concentrated and contemplated (by normal eyes, wisdom eyes, and Jhānacakkhu). We looked intensely (with anger). See - Upanijjhāyati.
upanijjhāyissanti: [Upa+ni+jhe+ssanti] (kri) CL=7 We will intensely concentrate and contemplate. We will intensely concentrate and contemplate (by normal eyes, wisdom eyes, and Jhānacakkhu). We will look intensely. See - Upanijjhanayati.
upanijjhāyita: [Upa+ni+jhe+ta] (ti) CL=7 Should be concentrated and contemplated.
upanijjhāyitabba: [Upa+ni+jhe+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be meditated or should be intensely concentrated and contemplated.
upanijjhāyiṃsu: [Upa+ni+jhe+iṃsu] (kri) CL=7 They meditated. They intensely concentrated and contemplated (by normal eyes, wisdom eyes, and Jhānacakkhu). They looked intensely (with anger). See - Upanijjhāyati.
upanijjhāyīyanti: [Upa+ni+jhe+ya+ante]  CL=9 That is approached and contemplated- recollected repeatedly.
upanikkhamanti: [Upa+ni+kamu+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They go out. They come out. See - Upanikkhamati.
upanikkhamassu: [Upa+ni+kamu+a+ssu] (kri) CL=7 May you come out. See - Upanikkhamati.
upanikkhami: [Upa+ni+kamu+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 I came out. See - Upanikkhamati.
upanikkhamiṃ: [Upa+ni+kamu+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 I came out. See - Upanikkhamati.
upanikkhepa: [Upa+ni+khipa+ṇa] (pu,na) CL=7 (1) Puts or places. (2) Enters. Puts in. Gets on well. (3) Compares. Considers. (Ti) (4) (A) (The wealth) that should be placed near. (The deposit wealth that concerns the wealth that is given to the Bank to get interest).
upanikkhepadhana: [Upanikkhepa+dhana] (na) CL=7 The wealth that is placed or deposited near (someone). The wealth that is a wager or stake or bet.
upanikkhepana: [Upa+ni+khipa+yu] (na) CL=7 Compare in a nearby place. Comparison. Compare and consider.
upanikkhipanta: [Upa+ni+khipa+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who places or deposits near.
upanikkhipanti: [Upa+ni+khipa+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They deposit near. See - Upanikkhipati-(B).
upanikkhipati: [Upa+ni+khipa+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 [Upanikpipati-saṃ] (A) Places. Puts down. Deposits near. (B) Places as an order.
upanikkhipeyya: [Upa+ni+khipa+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should place near. See - Upanikkhipati-(A).
upanikkhipitvā: [Upa+ni+khipa+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (A) Having placed down. Having deposited near. (A) Having put in. (B) Having considered.
upanikkhitta: [Upa+ni+khipa+ta] (ti) CL=7 (1) Placed down (in present and one"s back). Placed or deposited. (2) (The name or designation) that is named Upanikkhitta.
upanikkhittabhaṇḍa: [Upanikkhitta+bhaṇḍa] (na) CL=7 The wealth that is placed or deposited near.
upanikkhittabhaṇḍaṭṭhāniya: [Upanikkhittabhaṇḍa+ṭhāniya] (ti) CL=7 (The wealth) that is placed as deposited wealth.
upanikkhittaka: [Upanikkhitta+ka] (ti) CL=7 (1) (The wealth) that is kept and deposited. (2) (The name or designation) that is named Upanikkhitta.
upanikkhittakapaññatti: [Upanikkhittakā+paññatti] (thī) CL=7 The name or designation that is named Upanikkhitta. Considers or finds one and the next one is called two. Like that considers and finds two, the next one is called three, and so on. This is called Upanikkhittaka paññata.
upanikkhittapaññatti: [Upanikkhittā+paññatti] (thī) CL=7 The name or designation that is named Upanikkhitta. See - Upanikkhittakapaññatti.
upanikkhittasādiyana: [Upanīkkhitta+sādiyana] (na) CL=7 Enjoys or takes pleasure in the deposited wealth.
upanimantiyamāna: [Upa+ni+manta+ya+māna] (ti) CL=7 One who is invited respectfully.
upanipajjati: [Upa+ni+pada+ya+ti] (kri) CL=7 He lies down next (to). He sleeps. He crouches. He lies down.
upanipajjeyya: [Upa+ni+pada+ya+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should lie down next (to). He should sleep. He should crouch. He should lie down. See - Upanipajjati.
upanipajjissasi: [Upa+ni+pada+ya+ssasi] (kri) CL=7 He will lie down next (to). See - Upanipajjati.
upanipanna: [Upa+ni+pada+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who lies down near.
upanisasampanna: [Upanisā+sampanna] (ti) CL=7 One who is with the prerequisite or one who is completed with the dependent requisite.
upanisevati: [Upa+ni+seva+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 Clings onto. Wraps or binds onto.
upaniseveyya: [Upa+ni+seva+a+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should associate closely. He should cling (onto). See - Upanisevati.
upanisevita: [Upa+ni+seva+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who lives near or one who associates closely.
upanisinnaka: [Upanisinna+ka] (ti) CL=7 One who sits closely. See - Upanisinnakakathā.
upanisinnakakathā: [Upanisinnaka+kathā] (thī) CL=7 The dhamma words (sound) that are taught to one who sits near him.
upanisinnakaparikathā: [Upanisinnaka+parikathā] (thī) CL=7 The dhamma words (sound) that teach and see the condition/behavior of one who sits near him.
upanisinnakathā: [Upanisanna+kathā] (thī) CL=7 The dhamma words (sound) that are taught to one who sits near him. See - Upanisinnakakathā.
upanisinnaparisā: [Upanisinnā+parisā] (thī) CL=7 The audience who are sitting near him.
upanissaja: [Upa+ni+saja+a+hi] (kri) CL=7 May you give up or offer. See - Upanissajati.
upanissaya: [Upa+ni+si+a.(upanigraya-saṃ)] (pu) CL=7 (A) The strong decisive support. Upanissayapaccaya.  (B) The dwelling place and alms.
upanissayabala: [Upanissaya+bala] (na) CL=7 The power of strong decisive support.
upanissayabhājanīya: [Upanissaya+bhājanīya] (ti) CL=7 A section that is an analytical description of Upanissayapaccaya.
upanissayacittasantāna: [Upanissaya+cittasantāna] (na) CL=7 The sequence of mind that is the strong decisive support.
upanissayagocara: [Upanissaya+gocara] (pu) CL=7 The wandering place that is a strong decisive support of the quality such as virtues.
upanissayaindriya: [Upanissaya+indriya] (na) CL=7 The mental faculty that is a strong decisive support (of Ariyamagga).
upanissayakoṭi: [Upanissaya+koṭi] (thī) CL=7 The power of the decisive support. Makes first and foremost decisive support.
upanissayakoṭidassanamukha: [Upanissayakoṭi+dassanamukha] (na) CL=7 Makes first and foremost the top of decisive support.
upanissayakusala: [Upanissaya+kusala] (pu) CL=7 Merits that are strong decisive support that is Upanissayapaccaya.
upanissayakāraṇa: [Upanissaya+kāraṇa] (na) CL=7 A cause that is a strong decisive support or place.
upanissayalesa: [Upanissaya+lesa] (pu) CL=7 A hint of Upanissayapaccaya. Weak decisive support. See - Upanissasakoṭi.
upanissayamanda: [Upanissaya+manda] (ti) CL=7 Weak decisive support that is a cause of (attaining Magaphala). One who has weak wisdom.
upanissayaniddesa: [Upanissaya+niddesa] (pu) CL=7 A section that explains the analytical description of Upanissayapaccaya.
upanissayapaccaya: [Upanissaya+paccaya] (pu) CL=7 Upanissayapaccaya. Paccaya dhamma that is a supported dhamma which is a strong decisive support. See original.
upanissayapaccayadhamma: [Upanissāpaccaya+dhamma] (pu) CL=7 The decisive support nature or dhamma.
upanissayapaccayasabhāva: [Upanissāpaccaya+sabhāva] (pu) CL=7 The nature of decisive support.
upanissayapaccayasatti: [Upanissāpaccaya+satti] (thī) CL=7 The power of decisive support.
upanissayapamāṇa: [Upanissaya+pamāṇa]  CL=9 The extent of the perfection of great support of merit, the extent of the perfection of wholesome deed which is a great support.
upanissayapariyāya: [Upanissaya+pariyāya] (pu) CL=7 The synonym - an alternate term for the word - Upanissaya. The word that has the same meaning as Upanissaya.
upanissayapaṭikkhepa: [Upanissāya+paṭikkhepa] (pu) CL=7 Pāḷi that is a cause of removing decisive support.
upanissayarahita: [Upanissaya+rahita] (ti) CL=7 One who is free from strong decisive support.
upanissayasampadā: [Upanissaya+sampadā] (thī) CL=7 The fulfillment of strong decisive support (of attaining magga, phala).
upanissayasampanna: [Upanissaya+sampanna] (ti) CL=7 One who is fulfilled with strong decisive support. (In this status, strong decisive support that offered the requisites for monks (a lower robe, upper robe, double layer robe, monk"s bowl, razor, needle, monk"s girdle, and water filter), etc in the past).
upanissayasampatti: [Upanissaya+sampatti] (thī) CL=7 The fulfillment of decisive support which is tihetu such as a rebirth-linking state, etc., that is strong decisive support (of attaining magga, phala).
upanissayasampattipadaṭṭhāna: [Upanissaya+sampatti+padaṭṭhāna] (ti) CL=7 There is a proximate cause that is the fulfillment of strong decisive support.
upanissayasāmañña: [Upanissaya+sāmañña] (na) CL=7 As they are the same decisive support by upanissaya.
upanissayasīsa: [Upanissaya+sīsa] (na) CL=7 The head dhamma or lead dhamma that is Upanissayapaccaya.
upanissayavantu: [Upanissaya+vantu] (ti) CL=7 One who has strong decisive support.
upanissayavaṇṇanā: [Upanissaya+vaṇṇanā] (thī) CL=7 The commentary of the word - upanissaya.
upanissayavibhaṅga: [Upanissaya+vibhaṅga] (pu) CL=7 Pāḷi that explains the analytical description of Upanissayapaccaya.
upanissayavippanna: [Upanissaya+vipanna] (ti) CL=7 One who has strong decisive support that goes wrong.
upanissayindriya: [Upanissaya+indriya] (na) CL=7 The mental faculty that is strong decisive support.
upanissayābhāva: [Upanissaya+abhāva] (pu) CL=7 Lack of strong decisive support.
upanissayānurūpa: [Upanissaya+anurūpa] (ti) CL=7 In accordance with Upanissaya. In accordance with strong decisive support.
upanissita: [Upa+ni+si+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who is relying on.
upanissitabba: [Upa+ni+si+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be relied on or depended on.

upanāha: [Upa+naha+ṇa]  CL=7 Resentment is characterized by repeatedly binding the mind with anger, such as when a person blames or reproaches. It involves not giving up the anger. This state appears in the wisdom of a yogi as a characteristic of following after anger. In Pali, this is called kodha (initial anger) and upanāha (resentment). The anger that arises initially is called kodha, while the anger that arises repeatedly is called upanāha.

upanīyati:
[Upa+nī+ya+ti]  CL=7 (1) That which carries. (2) He is going toward old age (jarā) and death (maraṇa). (kammakata). (3) He causes one to reach old age (jarā) and death (maraṇa), effectively leading them there.
Upanīyati(kamma,kri) [upa+nī+ya+te].
upapada: [Upa+pada]  CL=7 (1) The word that occurs near the noun and verb is called the auxiliary word (upapada), or the word near the noun and verb. (Ti) (2) This word is typically accompanied by the main word.
upapadasamāsa: [Upapada+samāsa]  CL=7 The compound word associated with a near word is called upapada samāsa or nicca samāsa. It does not exist as a sentence, such as kumbhaṃ kāro, attato jo, urena go, or pādena po. Instead, it is always a permanent samāsa, such as kambhakāro, attajo, uraro, or pādapo. These are the nicca samāsa and kitanta samāsa, which are upapada samāsa.
upapadatthavisesa: [Upapada+attha+visesa] (pu) CL=7 The special meaning of a subordinate word.
upapajja:

upapajjissati: [Upa+pada+ya+ssati] (kri) CL=7 He will be reborn. He will reach ( the next existence). He will re-arise. He will be in the rebirth-linking state. See - Upapajjati.

upapatticitta: [Upapatti+citta] (na) CL=7 The mind that arises close to a new existence. Consciousness connection to rebirth-linking.

upasampannadivasa: [Upasampanna+divasa] (pu) CL=7 The day of becoming a monk.
upasampannakāla: [Upasampanna+kāla] (pu) CL=7 A period of becoming a higher ordained monk.
upasampannapubba: [Upasampanna+pubba] (ti) CL=7 One who is a monk in the past.
upasampannasamanantaraṃ: [Upasampanna+samanantaraṃ] (bya) CL=7 Goes beyond becoming a bhikkhu.
upasampannasaññī: [Upasampannasaññā+ī] (ti) CL=7 One who is perceiving (someone) as a higher ordained monastic.
upasampannasaṅkhya: [Upasampanna+saṅkhya] (thī,na) CL=7 The number of become a noble monk.
upasampannasikkhāsamādāna: [Upasampannasikkhā+samādāna] (na) CL=7 Undertaking Vinaya rules of Bhikkhu. See - Upasampadāpāripūrī.
upasamphusati: [Upa+saṃ+phusa+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 Comes close and touches. Upasamphusati(kā,kri) [upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+ti] Cause to touch.
upasamphuse:
[Upa+saṃ+phusa+eyya]  CL=7 (1) He would touch or contact. See - upasamphusati. (2) He should make contact.
Upasamphuse(kā,kri) [upa+saṃ+phusa+ṇe+eyya].
upasampādana: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+yu] (na) CL=7 Cause to complete. Cause to arise. Attain. See -  upasampadā.
upasampādanakāla: [Upasampādana+kāla] (pu) CL=7 A period of accomplishment of becoming (a monk). A period of becoming a monk.
upasampādayitvā: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇaya+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having caused to accomplish. Having caused to come to an end. See - Upasampajja-(2).
upasampādenta: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who makes to become a noble monk.
upasampādenti: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+anti] (kri) CL=7 They give higher ordination. See - Upasampādeti.
upasampādesi: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+si]  CL=8 Having ordained as a bhikkhu.. See - Upasampādeti.
upasampādessāma: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+ssāma]  CL=8 We will be ordained. See - Upasampādeti.
upasampādessāmi: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+ssāmi] (kri) CL=7 I will give a higher ordination.
upasampādetabba: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+tabba] (ti) CL=7 One who causes to accomplish and gives a higher ordination.
upasampādetha: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+tha] (kri) CL=7 You (pl) give higher ordination. See - Upasampādeti.
upasampādeti: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+ti] (kā,kri) CL=7 He causes a noble monk. He gives higher ordination. He ordains as a monastic.
upasampādetvā: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having given higher ordination or having become a noble monk.
upasampādeyya: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should give higher ordination. See - Upasampādeti.
upasampādita: [Upa+saṃ+pada+ṇe+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who should cause to accomplish and should give higher ordination.
upasampāditaantevāsika: [Upasampādita+antevāsika] (pu) CL=7 A disciple who should be ordained as a monastic.
upasamā: [Upa+samu+a+ā] (thī) CL=7 A bhikkhuni is named Upasamā.
upasamādhiṭṭhāna: [Upasama+adhiṭṭhāna] (na) CL=7 (1) The resolution dhamma that is having the calmness of kilesā. Upasamādhiṭṭhāna.
upasamādhiṭṭhānapariggahita: [Upasamādhiṭṭhāna+pariggahita] (ti) CL=7 Acquired by the resolution dhamma that is the calmness of kilesā.
upasamādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇa: [Upasamādhiṭṭhāna+paripūraṇa] (na) CL=7 The accomplishment of the establishment of peace.
upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgama: [Upasamādhiṭṭhāna+samudāgama] (pu) CL=7 Attains the establishment of peace.
upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgata: [Upasamādhiṭṭhāna+samudāgata] (ti) CL=7 Fulfilled the establishment of peace.
upasamānubrūhita: [Upasama+anubrūhita] (ti) CL=7 Developed by the cessation of kilesā.
upasamānussati: [Upasama+anussati] (thī) CL=7 Mindfulness that considers the quality of Nibbāna repeats again and again. Mindfulness that considers the quality of Ariyamagga repeats again and again. Upasamānussati. See - Upasama(ti)-(2, 3).
upasamāvaha: [Upasama+āvaha] (ti) CL=7 Leads to the state of cessation of suffering of cyclical existence.
upasanta: [Upa+samu+ta] (pu) CL=7 (1) Calmness. (2) One who is named Upasanta. (There are two persons who are named Upasanta. One who is a Thera is named Upasanta, a foremost disciple of Lord Buddha Atthadassī. Another one is a Thera named Upasanta a foremost disciple of Lord Buddha Vessabhū).
upasantadaratha: [Upasanta+daratha] (ti) CL=7 Anxiousness that has ceased. The cessation of anxiousness.
upasantadassana: [Upasanta+dassana]  CL=9 Seen peacefully- calmly; one (the Buddha). See upasantapatisa.
upasantakilesa: [Upasanta+kilesa] (ti) CL=7 With the ceased kilesā. See - Upasantasanta.
upasantakāraṇa: [Upasanta+kāraṇa] (na) CL=7 A cause of peace and tranquility.
upasantakāyavacīkammanta: [Upasanta+kāyavacīkammanta] (ti) CL=7 One who has calmed body action and oral action.
upasantapadissa: [Upasanta+pa+disa+a] (ti) CL=7 (Buddha) who is looking at peace and tranquility.
upasantapatisa: [Upasanta+pati+sama+kvi] (ti) CL=7 (Buddha) who is looking at peace and tranquility or (Buddha) who is looking respectfully of calm appearance.
upasantapatissa: [Upasanta+pati+sama+kvi] (ti) CL=7 (Buddha) who is looking at peace and tranquility or (Buddha) who is looking respectfully of calm appearance.
upasantarūpa: [Upasanta+rūpa] (ti) CL=7 One who has the characteristic of peace and tranquility.
upasantasabhāva: [Upasanta+sabhāva] (ti) CL=7 With the nature of calmness. One who has calmed behavior.
upasantasanta: [Upasanta+santa] (ti) CL=7 Calmness due to peace and tranquility. See - Upasantasantacitta.
upasantasantacitta: [Upasantasanta+citta] (ti) CL=7 The calm mind is due to peace and tranquility. With a calm mind. One who has a calm mind due to peace and tranquility.
upasantaussanna: [Upasanta+ussanna] (ti) CL=7 A higher calm state. One who has a very calm mind. See - Upasantapatisa.
upasantavacīsamācāra: [Upasanta+vacīsamācāra] (ti) CL=7 One who has a calm way of speaking or one who has a calm oral action.
upasantupasanta: [Upasanta+upasanta] (ti) CL=7 One who has abundant peace and tranquility.
upasantupasantaoḷārikabhāva: [Upasantupasanta+oḷārikabhāva] (pu) CL=7 As the calm state of the rough elements of Jhāna.
upasantūpasanta: [Upasanta+upasanta] (ti) CL=7 One who has calm behavior.
upasavanti: The word - Upasavanti comes from Upasanti.  Tipi, 4 B,400.
upasaṃbyāna: [Upa+saṃ+vī+yu] (na) CL=7 [Upari saṃ-vīyate pidhīyate bāhulyenāti, yu. Upasaṃpubbo vī tantasantāne. Dhāna, ṭī. 292.] A scarf or cloak. A towel.
upasaṃharanta: [Upa+saṃ+hara+anta] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī upasaṃharantī] One who comes close and concentrates.
upasaṃharanti: [Upa+saṃ+hara+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharantī: [Upa+saṃ+hara+anta+ī] (thī) CL=7 She brings (together) or comes close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharanta.
upasaṃharatha: [Upa+saṃ+hara+a+tha] (kri) CL=7 (You) (pl) bring together or you (pl) come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharati: [Upa+saṃ+hara+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He brings (together) or comes close to concentrate. (Saddattha). He causes. He bears in mind or meditates. He acts offering reverently. (Adhippāyattha).
upasaṃharatu: [Upa+saṃ+hara+a+tu] (kri) CL=7 May he bring (together) or come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharaṇa: [Upa+saṃ+hara+yu] (na) CL=7 Brings together  (Brings together one"s death by himself).
upasaṃharaṇābhāva: [Upasaṃharaṇa+abhāva] (pu) CL=7 Lack of bringing nearby or lack of concentration.
upasaṃharaṇākāra: [Upasaṃharaṇa+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner of bringing together.
upasaṃharaṇākāradassana: [Upasaṃharaṇakāra+dassana] (na) CL=7 Words (sound) that explain the manner of bringing together. Words (sound) of explanation of the manner of coming close and concentration.
upasaṃharaṇānukkama: [Upasaṃharaṇa+anukkama] (pu) CL=7 The sequence of bringing together or coming close and concentration.
upasaṃhareyya: [Upa+saṃ+hara+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should bring (together). See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃhari: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ī] (kri) CL=7 He brought (together) or coming close and concentration. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharissanti: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ssanti] (kri) CL=7 They will bring (together) or come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharissatha: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ssatha] (kri) CL=7 You (pl) will bring (together) or come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharissati: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ssati] (kri) CL=7 He will bring (together) or come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharitabba: [Upa+saṃ+hara+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be brought (together) or come close and concentrated.
upasaṃharitukāma: [Upasaṃharituṃ+kamu+ṇa] (ti) CL=7 One who wants to bring (together) or come close and concentrate..
upasaṃharitvā: [Upa+saṃ+hara+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having brought together or come close and concentrated.
upasaṃhariyamāna: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ya+māna] (ti) CL=7 Should be brought (together) or come close and concentrated.
upasaṃharāma: [Upa+saṃ+hara+a+ma] (kri) CL=7 Brings together or come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharāmi: [Upa+saṃ+hara+a+mi] (kri) CL=7 I bring (together) or come close and concentrate. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃharīyati: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ya+te] (kamma,kri) CL=7 Comes close and concentrates. Causes to focus.
upasaṃhaṭapesuñña: [Upasaṃhaṭa+pesuñña] (na) CL=7 A slander (words (sound)) that was brought (to).
upasaṃhita: [Upa+saṃ+dhā+ta] (ti) CL=7 Connected (with). Brought together or arose together.
upasaṃhāra: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 Brings together or comes close and concentrates. (saddattha). Bears in mind or concentrates and contemplates. Meditation. (adhippāyattha).
upasaṃhārattha: [Upasaṃhāra+attha] (ti) CL=7 The meaning of bringing (together) or concentration and contemplation.
upasaṃhāsi: [Upa+saṃ+hara+ī] (kri) CL=7 [Nirutti, nhā. 433.] Came close and concentrated. See - Upasaṃharati.
upasaṃvasati: [Upa+saṃ+vasa+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 Reveres. Comes close and lives. Depends on (something) for his livelihood.
upasaṃvase: [Upa+saṃ+vasa+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should revere. He should come close and live. He should depend on (something) for his livelihood. See - Upasaṃvasati.
upasaṃvaseyya: [Upa+saṃ+vasa+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should revere. He should come close and live. He should depend on (something) for his livelihood. See - Upasaṃvasati.
upasaṃyanti: [Upa+saṃ+yā+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They approach or come close.
upasaṅga: [Upa+sanja+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 Greed that clings (to) or attaches (on).
upasaṅgayha: [Upa+saṃ+gaha+tvā]  CL=9 Having seized properly with the manner of washing feet, smearing them (with ointment) and giving respect. (kū, sya).
upasaṅgaṇhitabba: [Upa+saṃ+gaha+ṇhā+tabba] (ti) CL=7 One who should be supported.
upasaṅkama: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+a+hi] (kri) CL=7 May you come close. May you approach. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamanakiriyā: [Upaṅsamana+kiriyā] (thī) CL=7 Making the action of coming close or approaching.
upasaṅkamanakāla: [Upasaṅkamana+kāla] (pu) CL=7 A period of approaching or coming close.
upasaṅkamanapariyosānadīpana: [Upasaṅkamanapariyosāna+dīpana] (thī,na) CL=7 Words (sound) that explain the action of approaching or coming close.
upasaṅkamanavara: [Upasaṅkamana+vara] (pu) CL=7 The gift or wish that is a chance of approaching or coming close. A wish or gift of a chance for approaching.
upasaṅkamanavidhāna: [Upasaṅkamana+vidhāna] (na) CL=7 An arrangement or plan of coming close and approaching.
upasaṅkamanaṭṭhāna: [Upasaṅkamana+ṭhāna] (na) CL=7 A place of approaching or visiting.
upasaṅkamanta: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+kanta] (ti) CL=7 One who approaches or comes close.
upasaṅkamantu: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+a+antu] (kri) CL=7 May they approach. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamanīya: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+anīya] (ti) CL=7 One who should be approached.
upasaṅkamati: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He goes near. He approaches. He comes close.
upasaṅkamatu: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+a+tu] (kri) CL=7 May he approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkameyya: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
[Upa+saṃ+kamu+eyyaṃ] (kri) CL=7 I should approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkameyyaṃ: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+eyyaṃ] (kri) CL=7 I should approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkameyyuṃ: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+eyyuṃ] (kri) CL=7 They should approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkameyyāma: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+eyyāma] (kri) CL=7 We should approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkami: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ī] (kri) CL=7 He approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
[Upa+saṃ+kamu+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 I approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamimhā: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+mhā] (kri) CL=7 We approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamissanti: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ssanti] (kri) CL=7 They will approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamissati: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ssati] (kri) CL=7 He will approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamissāma: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ssāma] (kri) CL=7 We will approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamissāmi: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ssāmi] (kri) CL=7 I will approach or come close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamita: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ta] (ti) CL=7 Approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamitaṭṭhāna.
upasaṅkamitabba: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+tabba] (na) CL=7 (1) Approaches or comes close. (Ti) See - Upasaṅkamitabbakāraṇa. (2) One who should be approached or come close.
upasaṅkamitabbakula: [Upasaṅkamitabba+kula] (na) CL=7 (A disciple) who should be approached (to). See - Upavajjakula.
upasaṅkamitabbakāraṇa: [Upasaṅkamitabba+kāraṇa] (na) CL=7 A cause of approaching or coming close.
upasaṅkamitabbayuttakāla: [Upasaṅkamitabbayutta+kāla] (pu) CL=7 A period of that is suitable to approach or come close.
upasaṅkamitabbaṭṭhāna: [Upasaṅkamitabba+ṭhāna] (na) CL=7 A place or (person) who is worth approaching or coming close.
upasaṅkamitaṭṭhāna: [Upasaṅkamita+ṭhāna] (na) CL=7 A place where (someone or an object) should be approached or come close.
upasaṅkamittha: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ttha]  CL=9 (They) approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamitukāma: [Upasaṅkamituṃ+kamu+ṇa] (ti) CL=7 One who wants to approach or come close.
upasaṅkamituṃ: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+tuṃ] (bya) CL=7 To approach or come close.
upasaṅkamitvā: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 Having approached or come close.
upasaṅkamiṃ: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+iṃ] (kri) CL=7 I approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkamiṃsu: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+uṃ] (kri) CL=7 They approached or came close. See - Upasaṅkamati.
upasaṅkanta: [Upa+saṃ+kamu+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who approaches or comes close.
upasaṅkappana: [Upa+saṃ+kappa+yu] (na) CL=7 (1) Comes close and contemplates. (Ti) See - Upasaṅkappananiyāma. (2) One who comes close, concentrates, and contemplates by wisdom. (Na).
upasaṅkappananiyāma: [Upasaṅkappana+niyāma] (pu) CL=7 The way of contemplation, The way that is how to contemplate.
upasaṅkheyya: [Upa+saṃ+khā+ṇya] (ti) CL=7 Which should be calculated or which should be counted.
upasaṅkhātabba: [Upa+saṃ+khā+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Which should be calculated or which should be counted.
upasaṭṭha: [Upa+saja(sajja)+ta] (na) CL=7 [Upasaṭa-saṃ.] (1) Afflicts or attaches. (Ti) (2) Should be given up. (3) Should be approached or come close. Completed or fulfilled. Upasaṭṭha(ti) [upa+sasu(sasa)+ta. Rū,nhā. 414. Nīti, dhā. 176. Dhātvattha. 394] (1) Which should be afflicted. One who is afflicted. Mixed with trouble or suffering. Enters to the trouble or suffering. (2) Afflicted. (2) See below word.
upasaṭṭharoga: [Upasaṭṭha+roga] (pu) CL=7 Disease that afflicts. Red rot Colletotrichuna falcatums (disease) of sugarcane.
upasaṭṭhākāra: [Upasaṭṭha+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner of affliction or attachment (on). See - Upasagga-(2).
upasena: [Yādicchakanāma] (pu,thī) CL=7 One who is named Upasena. (In sāsanā, there are 8 persons who are named Upasena, they are two Thera, one prince, and five women).
upasenadāraka: [Upasena+dāraka] (pu) CL=7 A young man is named Upasena.
upasenasutta: [Upasena+sutta] (na) CL=7 Upasenasutta. A sutta that is Lord Buddha utters words (sound) of joy which is based on Venerable Upasena.
upasenatthera: [Upasena+thera] (pu) CL=7 A Thera is named Upasena. In sāsanā, there are two Thera are named Upasena. One is a Thera Upasena who is a younger brother of Venerable Sāriputtarā. Another one is a Thera named Upasena who is a writer of Cūḷaniddesa+mahāniddesa aṭṭhakathā book.
upasenaāsīvisasutta: [Upasena+āsīvisa+sutta] (na) CL=7 A sutta that teaches about when Venerable Upasena is bitten by a snake, at that time, that sutta is the conversation between Venerable Sāriputtarā and Venerable Upasena.
upaseniya: [Upa+si+yu=upasena+ṇika] (ti) CL=7 One who used to sleep (in his mother"s bosom).
upaseveyya: [Upa+si+eyya] (kri) CL=7 He should revere or should associate (with). See - Upasevati.
upasevitabba: [Upa+si+tabba] (ti) CL=7 Should be associated or practiced.
upasevī: [Upa+si+ṇī] (ti) CL=7 One who used to associate or practice.
upasilesa: [Upa+silisa+a] (pu) CL=7 (1) Cling or attach. The meaning of a place of attachment. The meaning that is connected by close contact.
upasilesana: [Upa+silisa+yu] (na) CL=7 Attachment or affliction. See - Upasilesa.
upasiri: [Upa+siri] (thī) CL=7 A mansion is named Upasiri.
upasitta: [Upa+sica+ta]  CL=9 That is sprinkled or poured.
upasittavassa: [Upasitta+vassa]  CL=9 Having raindrops that is pouref- rained.
upasiva: [Yādicchakanāma] (pu) CL=7 One who is named Upasiva. In sāsanā, there are two persons who are named Upasiva. One is a Thera in 80 great disciples. See also - Upasiva.
upasivabrāhmaṇa: [Upasiva+brāhmaṇa] (pu) CL=7 A Brahmin is named Upasiva.
upasiṅghati: [Upa+sighi+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He approaches and sniffs. He smells or sniffs.
upasiṅghissati: [Upa+sighi+ssati] (kri) CL=7 He will sniff or smell. See - Upasiṅghati.
upasiṅghita: [Upa+sighi+ta] (ti) CL=7 One who sniffed or smelled.
upasiṅghiyamāna: [Upa+sighi+ya+māna] (ti) CL=7 Should be smelled or sniffed.
upasiṅghāpesi: [Upa+sighi+ṇāpe+ī] (kā,kri) CL=7 He made to sniff or smell. Poulticed a wound or sore. Caused to initiate. Applied eyedrops.
upasiṅghāyanta: [Upasiṅgha+āya+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who sniffs or smells (at).
upasobhana: [Upa+subha+ṇe+yu] (na) CL=7 Cause to beautiful or graceful. Ornament or decoration.
upasobhanta: [Upa+subha+anta] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī upasobhantī] Graceful or beautiful.
upasobhatha: [Upa+subha+ttha]  CL=9 ttha is changed to tha]was very graceful. See - Upasobhati.
upasobhati: [Upa+subha+a+ti] (kri) CL=7 He appears graceful or beautiful.

upassayasutta:
[Upassaya+sutta]  CL=10 Upasaya Sutta:
After the Buddha"s parinibbāna, Venerable Mahākassapa and Venerable Ānanda visited a bhikkhuni monastery. After Venerable Mahākassapa gave a Dhamma talk and departed, the bhikkhuni Thullatissā expressed her disapproval, saying:
'Why does Venerable Mahākassapa think it appropriate to teach Dhamma in the presence of the wise Venerable Ānanda? It"s like a needle-seller trying to sell needles to a needle-maker!'
Due to this incident, Venerable Mahākassapa addressed Venerable Ānanda, declaring his own qualities comparable to the Buddha"s. He then said:
'Whoever thinks they can obscure my six higher knowledges (abhiññā) is like someone thinking they can cover a seven-cubit elephant with a young palm leaf.'

upassaṭṭhasutta:
[Upassaṭṭha+sutta]  CL=10 This is a sutta where the Buddha teaches that when a noble disciple (ariyasāvaka) sees that:
- the eye (cakkhu)
- visual objects (rūpārammaṇa)
- eye-contact (cakkhusamphassa)
- feelings born of eye-contact (cakkhusamphassajā vedanā)
are all phenomena that are oppressed/afflicted, they develop disenchantment (nibbidā) with these elements. This disenchantment then leads progressively until they attain the fruit of Arahantship (arahattaphala).

upaññātasutta:
[Upaññāta+sutta]  CL=10 The Upannata Sutta:
In this sutta, the Buddha explains how he attained enlightenment and realized Nibbāna through two essential factors:
1. Never being satisfied with wholesome states (kusala dhamma) - meaning continuous effort to develop further spiritual progress
2. Unwavering persistence in meditation practice until attaining Arahantship, even if flesh and blood would dry up - not retreating from the practice until the goal is reached.

2. Nāḷi is a measurement unit used in ancient Magadha
3. According to the Sārattha Ṭīkā:

- Therefore, upaḍḍhanāḷi equals one palang (တစ်စလယ်)

[Uppajjana+vāra]  CL=10 Uppajjanavāra is one of the seven Great Chapters (Mahāvāra) that explains the latent defilements (anusaya) in three time periods:
- Those that have arisen (past)
- Those that are arising (present)
- Those that will arise (future)

uppanna:
[U+pada+ta]  CL=10 [U+panna] Translation:
1. Arising/Occurrence
2. That which has reached the three moments (uppāda-ṭhiti-bhaṅga) occurring after the dissolution moment of a previous (past) phenomenon, specifically:
a) That which has arisen
b) That which is obtained/attained
c) That which has emerged/risen
d) That which is inseparable
e) That which is not yet cut off/eliminated
f) That which has reached the three moments (arising, presence, dissolution)
g) That which is currently arising/in the process of arising
h) That which will arise/is suitable to arise
3. Place of arising/occurrence
4. That which is caused to arise
5. A phenomenon similar to one that has already arisen

[U+pata+ṇa]  CL=9 Uppāta (or Uppāda) is that which manifests and proceeds to show good and bad results [according to the Commentary]. It consists of: 1. Omens, signs, portents and phenomena including:
- Lunar eclipses
- Solar eclipses
- Meteors/falling stars
- Directional phenomena/disturbances
(These are called Uppāta-titta-nimitta when great elements show signs of good or bad results. The five great Uppāta are: lunar eclipse, solar eclipse, stellar conjunctions, falling of great stars, and directional disturbances/phenomena [Reference: Jā.Ṭṭha.1.396]. There are also many minor omens and signs.)
2. Knowledge related to:
- Echo phenomena
- Directional disturbances
- Earthquakes
- Other related arts of interpreting omens and signs
3. The contemplation and consideration of these omens and signs

- They are taken as qualities (like color, etc.) of the great element

upādānaparipavattasutta:
[Upādāna+paripavatta+sutta]  CL=9 This is a sutta where the Buddha declares that only when one thoroughly understands the four aspects of clinging (upadana), can one claim to have attained Omniscient Knowledge (sabbaññuta-ñāṇa). The four aspects are:
1. Understanding form (rupa)
2. Understanding the cause of form
3. Understanding the cessation of form
4. Understanding the path leading to the cessation of form
The Buddha teaches that only one who understands these aspects becomes:
- Well-established in the sasana (Buddhist teaching)
- Liberated from defilements (kilesa)
- One who has completed all spiritual tasks
The same pattern of understanding applies to the other four aggregates: feeling (vedana), perception (sañña), mental formations (sankhara), and consciousness (viññāṇa).'
This sutta emphasizes the importance of thoroughly understanding the nature of clinging through these four aspects for complete liberation. It"s worth noting that this systematic understanding of the five aggregates (khandhas) is crucial for achieving enlightenment.

upādāniyasutta:
[Upādāniya+sutta]  CL=9 1. First Upadaniya Sutta (SN 22.121):
- Teaches that the five aggregates (khandhas) are things that can be clung to (upadaniya)
- Defines attachment (upadana) as the desire and passion for these five aggregates
- In the Pali Canon, the Buddha uses the phrase "upadaniyesu dhammesu"
- The commentator (Tika) named it Upadaniya Sutta based on this usage
2. Second Upadaniya Sutta (SN 35.123):
